title: Consolidate the full generation pipeline end-to-end (terrain seed -> water -> quantization -> terrain WFC -> buildings -> interiors -> manual/freeform), and answer who authors tile modules and whether a wall can bypass the system
objective: Owner said the individual pieces (Townscaper-style buildings, terrain elevation, water/rivers) are each understood on their own, but how they fit together end to end, and who actually defines each tile module, and what happens if someone wants to build a wall outside the system, are still unclear. This synthesizes already-recorded findings (no new external research needed) into one concrete, ordered pipeline: (1) noise-rs generates a continuous heightmap seed; (2) flow-accumulation runs on that continuous seed to produce a water mask (rivers/lakes) before any quantization, per the already-recorded 'Water and rivers' section; (3) the continuous heightmap+water mask are quantized into the discrete stacked-layer grid the WFC systems operate on, per the already-recorded 'Terrain elevation' section; (4) the terrain-block WFC tileset resolves non-water discrete cells into actual terrain geometry; (5) water cells get a Three.js Water/WaterMesh plane instead of terrain geometry, at the locally-appropriate height; (6) the exterior/building WFC tileset (Townscaper-style) resolves on top of buildable terrain cells; (7) a further WFC pass with an interior-specific tileset resolves each building floor's room layout, per the already-recorded 'Interior generation' section; (8) manual/freeform construction (Tier 1) sits on top of all of the above. Also answers, using this session's own prior Townscaper research plus TaleSpire's reference-table entry (already recorded: 'freeform, non-gridded decor props' alongside hard-grid structural tiles), who actually authors each WFC tile module (a real, hand-modeled 3D-asset content-creation task tagging each module with socket/adjacency metadata for ghx_proc_gen -- not something generated automatically), and surfaces, without resolving, a genuine fork for a wall built outside the tileset system: Option 1, everything structural must be an authored tileset module (consistent but limited to authored shapes), vs. Option 2, TaleSpire-style freeform structural props that bypass the WFC tileset entirely but then need their mechanical properties (collision via parry, vision-blocking) manually attached rather than inherited automatically from tileset metadata.
validations: Added a 'How the generation pipeline fits together, end to end' section to docs/research/vtt-map-and-terrain-construction-options.md with the 8-step ordered pipeline connecting every already-recorded piece (heightmap seed, water/flow-accumulation, quantization, terrain WFC, building WFC, interior WFC, manual/freeform), cross-referencing each step to the section that already documents it rather than duplicating content.

Added a 'Who authors each tile module, and can a wall bypass the system?' section: states plainly that tile modules are hand-authored 3D assets tagged with adjacency metadata (a real content-creation task, connecting to the still-open asset-pipeline item), and surfaces the structural-vs-freeform fork (Option 1: everything structural is an authored module; Option 2: TaleSpire-style freeform structural props with manually-attached mechanical properties) as a genuine open decision, not resolved unilaterally.
Updated docs/research/vtt-product-scope-map.md's Content Creation section to reference the tile-authoring reality now made explicit.
This is a synthesis of already-recorded findings -- no new WebSearch/WebFetch calls were needed or made.
No dependency installed, no code written, no ADR reopened -- documentation consolidation only.
risks: The structural-vs-freeform fork is presented with options, not resolved -- a real open decision remains for the owner.
